postings.description:
About Us

Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.

We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. About the Role

We are looking for an Applied Scientist to solve challenging and open-ended problems in the domain of Creators and content contextual signals. As an Applied Scientist on Twitch's GTM Science team, you will use applied machine learning to tackle ambiguous business problems across problem areas such as Ads, Brand Safety, Creator Sponsorship and Content Understanding. You will lead high profile projects where you will use a wide toolbox of ML tools to handle multiple types of data, including user behavior, metadata, and user generated content such as text and video. You will collaborate with a team of passionate scientists, engineers, and product stakeholders to develop these models, prototype and put them into production, where they can help Twitch's creators and viewers succeed and build communities.

You will report to our Senior Data Science Manager for GTM. This position is located in San Francisco, CA.

You Will:

- Build machine learning products to enrich Twitch’s content understanding and help creators and viewers build and discover their communities. 

- Propose, design, and oversee execution for high-impact projects that work backwards from customer problems to develop the right solution for the job. Know when to use a classical ML model versus a state-of-the-art one.

- Collaborate with cross-functional engineering and product teams to prototype and deploy your models into flexible data pipelines and ML-based services.

- Bring innovation and help drive science culture on the team by staying up to date and experimenting with new techniques in LLM, computer vision, inference and model evaluation.

- Experience owning projects that involve numerous scientists and engineers.

- Experience working with both technical and non-technical partners and stakeholders.

- Expertise with: Python and SQL, modern open source ML libraries (Pytorch, Tensorflow, etc.). Developing software in AWS or similar cloud-computing services.

- PhD with a specialization in Machine Learning.

- Experience with computer vision, LLM inference, content understanding. 

- 1+ years of experience working in GTM / Content / Creator orgs (not necessarily as a scientist).

- Familiarity with Twitch, its business, and its community.

postings.description:

About the Team

Twitch is all about community, and our Community team is a core pillar of what makes Twitch, Twitch. Community Discovery & ML (CDML) helps millions of viewers find the creators and communities they'll love. That covers search, browse, the mobile live and clips feeds, recommended notifications, and the recommendation systems behind them. When a viewer finds a new creator through one of these, it's often the start of a lasting connection. That connection is what keeps viewers, and the creators they watch, coming back.

About the Role

We're looking for a data scientist with strong statistics and modeling skills to be the science partner for the machine learning and recommendation systems behind Twitch's discovery products. You will work with product managers, ML engineers and applied scientists to help build what our recommendation systems should optimize for. That means balancing what a viewer does today (a click, a play, minutes watched) against what keeps them coming back: return visits, daily habits, and lasting connections with creators. It also means weighing short-form clips against long-form live content, and each surface against the others. This role will draw from a variety of statistical learning techniques, causal inference, optimization and recommender systems evaluation, and it still owns the full path from question to decision.

Reporting to the Director of Data Science, you will work from our San Francisco, CA office.

You Will:

- Help define the objective functions and success metrics for ranking and recommendations across feeds, search and notifications. Make the trade-offs explicit between short-term engagement (clicks, plays, watch time) and long-term outcomes (return visits, retention, new creator connections), including how short-form clips and live content add to or take away from each other.

- Evaluate ranking, recommendation and feed changes with ML engineers and applied scientists. This covers A/B tests and long-running holdouts, offline metrics that predict online results, and the cost and value of exploration and cold start. Handle the hard cases: novelty effects, interference between experiments, two-sided marketplace effects involving creators and viewers, and feedback loops in recommendation data.

- Build statistical and ML models that explain viewer behavior and size opportunities, such as propensity, uplift, survival and retention models. Include proxy metrics that predict long-term retention, so teams can decide in days rather than months.

- Turn ambiguous product questions into clear analyses. Quantify the uncertainty, and make recommendations that inform the machine learning and discovery roadmap.

- Define the logging and data needed to measure discovery surfaces, and check its quality.

- Contribute to the team's standards for experimentation, causal inference and model evaluation, and share what you learn with other data scientists.

You Have:

- A BA/BS in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Science or a related quantitative field, or equivalent industry experience.

- 3+ years as a data scientist in a high-velocity, data-driven environment, with hands-on experience applying statistical modeling and machine learning (regression, classification, causal inference, time series), including the assumptions behind each method and when it fails.

- Experience designing and analyzing online experiments, including variance reduction, power analysis and the pitfalls of interpreting results.

- Expert SQL and proficiency in Python or R.

- A track record of using data and models to influence product decisions and leadership.

Bonus Points

- An MS or PhD in a quantitative field.

- Experience with recommender systems, search ranking or feed ranking, such as offline evaluation (precision and recall, NDCG), exploration versus exploitation, or cold-start problems.

- Experience with multi-objective optimization or with defining objective functions for ranking systems, including choosing weights between competing goals.

- Experience building proxy metrics for long-term outcomes, or estimating long-term effects from long-running holdouts or observational data (e.g., difference-in-differences, synthetic control, uplift modeling).

- Experience with two-sided platforms or marketplaces, where changes for viewers also affect creators or supply.

- Experience on a consumer content platform: streaming, short-form video, social or marketplaces.

- Familiarity with Twitch, as a viewer or a creator (or both!).

- Track employee engagement and feedback, using what you learn to make our communications more useful and effective.

Own All Hands

- Lead All Hands programming, including editorial strategy and content development.

- Work closely with production and creative partners on run of show, speaker prep, creative elements, and live production.

- Build relationships across the company to uncover great stories, interesting speakers, and work employees should know about.

- Develop new segments and formats that keep All Hands fresh, engaging, and worth employees’ time.

- Think creatively about how All Hands can evolve. We want someone who sees it as programming—not just a company meeting—and has ideas for making it better.

- You’re a strong project manager and producer who can keep multiple timelines moving at once — delivering weekly programming while planning for what’s ahead. postings.title: Undergrad Software Engineering Intern (Grad Year: Spring 2028)
postings.description:
Please apply to this job with your personal email address (not your University or Program account) to avoid important Twitch emails hitting your spam inbox.

About Us:

Launched in 2011, Twitch is a global community that comes together each day to create multiplayer entertainment: unique, live, unpredictable experiences created by the interactions of millions. We bring the joy of co-op to everything, from casual gaming to world-class esports to anime marathons, music, and art streams. Twitch also hosts TwitchCon, where we bring everyone together to celebrate, learn, and grow their personal interests and passions. We’re always live at Twitch. Stay up to date on all things Twitch on Linkedin, X and on our Blog.

About the Role

**This internship is only for undergraduate students at North American colleges/universities with Spring 2028 graduation dates. We understand these can be flexible, so if that's the case, you can indicate on the application that you'd like to be considered for both. No need to apply to both roles.**

At Twitch, we’re always looking for high-potential talent. If you’re a current student in computer science, we’d love to see you apply. See below for just a few reasons why our cohort-based internship program is one-of-a kind.

Project-Based Learning at Scale: Twitch operates at a massive scale, requiring us to push the boundaries of technology and experiment with techniques used by only the largest websites. As an intern, you’ll have the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging engineering problems in the industry, making every project a valuable learning experience. 

Comprehensive Support Team: To ensure our interns thrive, we provide a dedicated support system, including a Manager, Mentor, and Early Careers Advisor. This team will work closely with you to guide your project from start to finish and ensure you have the resources needed to succeed. 

Enriched Intern Community: In addition to hands-on engineering work, you will participate in leadership and interpersonal development curriculum, as well as gain valuable industry insights from Twitch leaders through fireside chats. To complement the technical aspects of the program, we offer a variety of enrichment activities, including cohort trips, weekly advisory sessions, and local community events. We also provide housing assistance to make your summer internship as rewarding and enjoyable as possible.

Want to learn more? Check out the Early Careers Page for internship and student-focused content. 

You can work from San Francisco, CA.

You Will:

- Contribute to product design and implementation discussions

- Find and build unique solutions to implement projects from the idea phase to production

- Test and iterate code before and after production release

- Connect with intern peers, new teammates, and colleagues from across the business

You Have:

- BA/BS Graduation Year: Spring/Summer 2028. No Masters/PhD

- Eagerness to investigate challenges and present reasonable solutions reliably and quickly 

- Excitement to pick up a new language and be productive with it in a week 

- Desire to work collaboratively in a team environment 

- Completed coursework in or have an understanding of Data Structures and Algorithms

Perks

- Housing Stipend provided 

- Relocation assistance to and from San Francisco, CA

- Free Snacks & Beverages

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at Twitch. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several US geographic markets. The base pay for this position ranges from $42.5/hr in our lowest geographic market up to $88.94/hr in our highest geographic market. Pay is based on a number of factors including market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Amazon is a total compensation company. Dependent on the position offered, equity, sign-on payments, and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package, in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits. For more information, please visit https://www.aboutamazon.com/workplace/employee-benefits. Applicants should apply via our internal or external career site.

Twitch is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Twitch values your privacy. Please consult our Candidate Privacy Notice, for information about how we collect, use, and disclose personal information of our candidates.
